name: DISABLE AUTOMATIC UPDATES
description: Applies the NoAutoUpdate policy: Windows Update stops downloading and installing updates on its own. Manual checks and installs still work. Fully honored on Pro/Enterprise.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -Name 'NoAutoUpdate' -ErrorAction Stop).NoAutoUpdate; if ($v -eq 1) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: NOTIFY BEFORE DOWNLOAD
description: Puts automatic updates into notify-only mode (AUOptions=2): updates are offered, but nothing is downloaded or installed without your approval.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -Name 'AUOptions' -ErrorAction Stop).AUOptions; if ($v -eq 2) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: NO AUTO-RESTART WHILE SIGNED IN
description: Blocks automatic restarts for update installation while a user is signed on. Updates can still install, but the restart waits for you.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU' -Name 'NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers' -ErrorAction Stop).NoAutoRebootWithLoggedOnUsers; if ($v -eq 1) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: MAXIMUM ACTIVE HOURS (00:00-23:00)
description: Pins active hours to the whole day (policy) so Windows never restarts for updates while you are working.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU'; $a = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'SetActiveHours' -ErrorAction Stop).SetActiveHours; $s = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'ActiveHoursStart' -ErrorAction Stop).ActiveHoursStart; $e = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'ActiveHoursEnd' -ErrorAction Stop).ActiveHoursEnd; if ($a -eq 1 -and $s -eq 0 -and $e -eq 23) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DEFER FEATURE UPDATES 365 DAYS
description: Delays big Windows version upgrades for up to 365 days via the Update-for-Business policy. Pro/Enterprise feature; ignored on Home.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate'; $f = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'DeferFeatureUpdates' -ErrorAction Stop).DeferFeatureUpdates; $d = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'DeferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays' -ErrorAction Stop).DeferFeatureUpdatesPeriodInDays; if ($f -eq 1 -and $d -eq 365) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DEFER QUALITY UPDATES 30 DAYS
description: Delays monthly quality/security updates for up to 30 days via the Update-for-Business policy. Pro/Enterprise feature; ignored on Home.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate'; $f = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'DeferQualityUpdates' -ErrorAction Stop).DeferQualityUpdates; $d = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'DeferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays' -ErrorAction Stop).DeferQualityUpdatesPeriodInDays; if ($f -eq 1 -and $d -eq 30) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: PIN CURRENT WINDOWS VERSION
description: Locks feature updates to the Windows version installed right now (read at apply time). New builds stop being offered until you unpin.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate'; $t = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'TargetReleaseVersion' -ErrorAction Stop).TargetReleaseVersion; $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'TargetReleaseVersionInfo' -ErrorAction Stop).TargetReleaseVersionInfo; $cur = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion').DisplayVersion; if ($t -eq 1 -and $v -eq $cur) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: PAUSE UPDATES - 35 DAYS
description: Native pause: feature and quality updates are suspended for 35 days (timestamps are computed when you apply). Alternative to PAUSE UNTIL 2099 - both share the same pause stamps, so only the one applied last is in effect. Undo removes all pause stamps.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $e = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings' -Name 'PauseQualityUpdatesEndTime' -ErrorAction Stop).PauseQualityUpdatesEndTime; $d = [datetime]::Parse($e); $n = Get-Date; if ($d -gt $n -and $d -lt $n.AddDays(60)) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: PAUSE UPDATES UNTIL 2099
description: Sets every pause timestamp to year 2099 - effectively no automatic updates until then. A hard freeze. Alternative to PAUSE 35 DAYS - both share the same pause stamps, so only the one applied last is in effect. Undo removes all pause stamps.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings' -Name 'PauseUpdatesExpiryTime' -ErrorAction Stop).PauseUpdatesExpiryTime; if ($v -match '2099') { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: EXTEND MAX PAUSE WINDOW (10 YEARS)
description: Raises the maximum pause window Windows accepts (FlightSettingsMaxPauseDays=3650). Companion switch for the long pauses above.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings' -Name 'FlightSettingsMaxPauseDays' -ErrorAction Stop).FlightSettingsMaxPauseDays; if ($v -ge 3650) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: LOCK WINDOWS UPDATE SETTINGS PAGE
description: Applies DisableWindowsUpdateAccess: the Windows Update controls in Settings are hidden/blocked and show managed-by-organization text.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -Name 'DisableWindowsUpdateAccess' -ErrorAction Stop).DisableWindowsUpdateAccess; if ($v -eq 1) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: BLOCK DRIVER UPDATES VIA WU
description: Stops Windows Update from offering driver updates: excludes WU drivers from quality updates and removes WU from the driver search order.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $e = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate' -Name 'ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate' -ErrorAction Stop).ExcludeWUDriversInQualityUpdate; $s = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\DriverSearching' -Name 'SearchOrderConfig' -ErrorAction Stop).SearchOrderConfig; if ($e -eq 1 -and $s -eq 0) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DELIVERY OPTIMIZATION - NO P2P (HTTP ONLY)
description: Forces Delivery Optimization into HTTP-only mode: no peer-to-peer uploading of update chunks to other PCs, on your LAN or the internet.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization' -Name 'DODownloadMode' -ErrorAction Stop).DODownloadMode; if ($v -eq 0) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: SET ETHERNET + WIFI AS METERED
description: Marks wired and wireless networks as metered so Windows throttles background downloads. Affects Store and Delivery Optimization traffic too.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\NetworkList\DefaultMediaCost'; $e = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'Ethernet' -ErrorAction Stop).Ethernet; $w = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name 'WiFi' -ErrorAction Stop).WiFi; if ($e -eq 2 -and $w -eq 2) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: BLOCK AUTO-DOWNLOADS ON METERED NETWORKS
description: Even security updates stop auto-downloading over metered connections (AllowAutoWindowsUpdateDownloadOverMeteredNetwork=0). Combine with the metered switch above.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings' -Name 'AllowAutoWindowsUpdateDownloadOverMeteredNetwork' -ErrorAction Stop).AllowAutoWindowsUpdateDownloadOverMeteredNetwork; if ($v -eq 0) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DON'T GET UPDATES AS SOON AS POSSIBLE
description: Opts out of the aggressive fast rollout (IsContinuousInnovationOptedIn=0): updates arrive on the normal cadence instead of day-one.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\WindowsUpdate\UX\Settings' -Name 'IsContinuousInnovationOptedIn' -ErrorAction Stop).IsContinuousInnovationOptedIn; if ($v -eq 0) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DISABLE WINDOWS UPDATE SERVICE
description: Stops and disables the wuauserv service - the strongest single switch. Windows may silently repair it via its update medic service within minutes (by design); press CHECK STATE to see the live truth and re-apply if needed. Undo restores manual start.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $s = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\wuauserv' -Name 'Start' -ErrorAction Stop).Start; if ($s -eq 4) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DISABLE UPDATE ORCHESTRATOR (USOSVC)
description: Stops and disables the Update Orchestrator service, the component that schedules update scans and install windows.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $s = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\UsoSvc' -Name 'Start' -ErrorAction Stop).Start; if ($s -eq 4) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"

name: DISABLE UPDATE MEDIC (WAASMEDICSVC)
description: Stops the service whose job is to repair Windows Update back to health - the piece that often re-enables everything above. Undo restores manual start.
check: powershell -NoProfile -Command "try { $s = (Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\WaaSMedicSvc' -Name 'Start' -ErrorAction Stop).Start; if ($s -eq 4) { exit 0 } else { exit 1 } } catch { exit 1 }"
